summary: Clarence Linton Meader was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan (A.B. ~1887–1891), Athens, Bonn, Munich, and Rome, later serving as Instructor in Latin at the University of Michigan (1893–1938).

Claude Charles Fauriel worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Alexander Hamilton (~1802–1806) and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He co-founded the Société Asiatique and held posts at the Sorbonne (Professor of Foreign Literature, 1830) and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (1831).

Linguist Claude Hagège studied at the École Normale Supérieure, ENLOV, and under André Martinet (1971). His career included posts at the CNRS (~1965–1970), University of Poitiers (1970–1987), EPHE (~1978–1982), and Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques was an epigraphist and historian of Indology who studied under Armand Minard (~1958–1962) and George Cœdès (~1960–1969). He directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1963–1973) and taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1973–1999).

Claude Lévi-Strauss studied law at Paris (~1927–1931) and under Marcel Mauss (~1930–1934). He held posts at the University of São Paulo (~1935–1939), EPHE (~1950–1974), EHESS (~1950–1975), and the Collège de France (1959–1982).

Claude-Auguste Court was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Lycée de Casale, École Polytechnique, and Saint-Cyr (~1812–1813), and served as an engineer officer for the Sikh Khalsa Army and Ranjit Singh's court (~1827–1843).

Claudia Benthien is a scholar of linguistics and other fields. She earned degrees from Washington University and Humboldt University of Berlin (Dr. phil. 1997; Habilitation 2004), later becoming a Full Professor at the University of Hamburg (2005).

Claudia Dellacasa works in Buddhist studies and related fields. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (MA 2017) and Durham University (PhD 2021). She held fellowships at Tübingen and UCD (2022–2024) before becoming Lecturer at the University of Glasgow (2024).
Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Claudie Marcel-Dubois worked in Indology and ethnomusicology, studying at the Conservatoire de Paris and the EPHE under Marcel Mauss and Paul Masson-Oursel (~1933–1939). She held posts at MNATP (1937–1981) and the EPHE (from 1961).

Claudine Bautze-Picron is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Jean Naudou and was affiliated with the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2008).

Claudio Cicuzza is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been affiliated with Webster University (attested 2011) and served as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Claudio Giacomino was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held teaching posts at Liceo Chiabrera-Martini and Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio as Ordinary Professor of Latin and Greek literature.

Claudius Buchanan was a scholar of religious studies and Indology educated at the University of Glasgow (1782–1784) and Queens' College, Cambridge (B.A. 1795). He worked for the Church Mission Society (1797–1808) and served as Vice-Provost at Fort William College.
Claus Haebler was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Friedrich Weller (~1950–1955) and Paul Thieme. He held a post at the University of Münster from ~1972 to 1999.

Claus Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, completing his PhD (~1973) and Habilitation (~1983) at the University of Hamburg. He taught at Hamburg (~1974–1986) and headed the Department of Indology at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

Claus Vogel was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Marburg and Deccan College. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (1959–1976), University of Bonn (1976–1998), and University of Göttingen (1971; 1989).
Clemency Montelle is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She has held posts at the University of Canterbury, including Associate Professor in 2007 and a position from 2020 to 2025.

Clemens a Jesu was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the Urban College until 1756. He served in the Archdiocese of Verapoly (~1757–1782) and was Vicar General of the Malabar Mission in 1774.

Clements Markham was a historian and Tibetologist educated at Cheam and Westminster School. He served as Secretary (1863–1888) and President (1893–1905) of the Royal Geographical Society, held leadership roles at the Hakluyt Society, and worked at the India Office.
